prompts.title: Bid qualification: go or no-go
prompts.summary: An invitation to bid lands and you need a defensible recommendation before you spend a week estimating it.

prompts.title: Constructability risk review of a drawing set
prompts.summary: You are pricing or planning a job and want a structured list of buildability questions before the bid goes in.

prompts.title: Programme and sequencing options
prompts.summary: You have a target completion date and a rough scope, and you want the plausible sequencing options on the table before you build a CPM schedule.

prompts.title: Unit rate sanity check
prompts.summary: An estimate is nearly finished and you want a second pair of eyes on whether the rates and quantities hang together — before the bid goes in, not after.

prompts.title: Takeoff review checklist
prompts.summary: A takeoff has been produced — by a person, by software, or by one of the tools in our [open source construction tools](https://github.com/constructelligence-lab/open-source-construction-tools) list — and it needs a review that is actually systematic.

prompts.title: Change order pricing narrative
prompts.summary: The numbers are agreed internally and now need to be presented so they are hard to argue with — typically for a priced change that a client or a subcontractor will scrutinise.

prompts.title: Productivity assumption stress test
prompts.summary: An estimate depends on production rates you have assumed rather than measured, and you want to know how much of the margin is riding on them.

prompts.title: Design brief from a client conversation
prompts.summary: You have come out of a client meeting with scattered notes and need a written brief that the client can confirm or correct before design work starts.

prompts.title: Specification section draft
prompts.summary: You need a first draft of a specification section structure so you are editing rather than staring at an empty document — with the understanding that the technical content is yours, not the model's.

prompts.title: Code and accessibility checklist for a design review
prompts.summary: You want a structured set of compliance questions to work through for a design, recognising that the model does not know your local code and must not be treated as knowing it.

prompts.title: Design review agenda that finds problems
prompts.summary: You are running a design or coordination review and want an agenda that surfaces conflicts rather than walking through the drawings in order.

prompts.title: Photorealistic exterior render prompt
prompts.summary: You need a client-ready exterior visual quickly, before the model is advanced enough for a proper render, or to explore a façade direction.

prompts.title: Interior render: iteration prompt
prompts.summary: The first interior image is close but wrong — the light, the proportions or the materials — and you want to change one thing at a time rather than regenerate from scratch.

prompts.title: Render critique before it goes to the client
prompts.summary: You are about to send a visual to a client and want a hard critique first — one that finds the things an architect, a planner or a contractor would spot immediately.

prompts.title: Structural load path sanity check
prompts.summary: You are preparing for a coordination or value-engineering discussion and want the obvious load path and stability questions on the table.

prompts.title: MEP coordination and clash triage
prompts.summary: You have a clash report or a coordination problem list and need to decide which clashes matter, in what order to resolve them, and who should move.

prompts.title: Schedule narrative for the owner
prompts.summary: The monthly schedule update is done and needs the narrative section: what moved, why, what you are doing about it, and what you need — without excuses and without jargon.

prompts.title: Three-week lookahead constraint sweep
prompts.summary: You are building the next three-week lookahead and want to remove constraints before they stop work, rather than reporting them after the fact.

prompts.title: Daily report from messy field notes
prompts.summary: The day's notes are a mix of texts, voice-note reminders and scribbles, and the report needs to be written before you go home — with the facts intact and nothing invented.

prompts.title: RFI drafting that gets answered
prompts.summary: Something on site does not match the drawings and you need an RFI that is clear enough to be answered first time, with the schedule impact stated.

prompts.title: Job safety analysis from a task description
prompts.summary: You are preparing a task-specific safety analysis and want a structured first draft to edit with the crew, rather than starting from a template that says nothing about this job.

prompts.title: Toolbox talk from a real near miss
prompts.summary: Something nearly went wrong on this site and you want a five-minute talk that lands with the crew, rather than a generic briefing they have heard ten times.

prompts.title: Contract risk review preparation
prompts.summary: A contract or subcontract is on your desk and you want the risk topics organised before it goes to your lawyer, so the expensive hours are spent on judgement rather than on reading out loud.

prompts.title: Notice letter draft
prompts.summary: An event has occurred and the contract requires written notice.

prompts.title: Project case study from the facts
prompts.summary: You have finished a job worth writing about and need a case study for the website, a proposal or a prequalification pack — without inventing anything and without breaching confidentiality.

prompts.title: Tailoring a proposal to the client's actual concerns
prompts.summary: You have a standard proposal structure and a specific client, and you want the document to answer what *they* are worried about instead of repeating your company history.

prompts.title: IFC data extraction script
prompts.summary: You need a repeatable way to pull data out of IFC models — quantities, spaces, properties — instead of clicking through them, and you would rather review code than write the boilerplate.

prompts.title: Job cost analysis in Python or pandas
prompts.summary: Your accounting system will give you a job cost export but not the analysis you want, and the work is repetitive enough to script rather than rebuild in a spreadsheet every month.
